sources.work: Praśna Mārga (pūrvārdha, chapters 1-16) with the Sanskrit notes of Punnasseri Nambi Neelakantha Sarma
sources.author: Nārāyaṇan Nampūtiri of Panakkāṭṭu (composed 1649 CE); edited by Punnasseri Nambi Neelakantha Sarma (1858-1934)
sources.workStatus: Public domain. The work is of 1649. The 1926 edition's editor died in 1934, so his notes have been public domain in India since 1 January 1995 (life + 60); US: published 1926, before 1931.
sources.edition: Praśnamārga, ed. Punnasseri Nambi Neelakantha Sarma, 1926 (archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.332036), pūrvārdha
sources.licence: Digital Library of India scan 2015.332036 of a 1926 printed edition. No rights statement on the item; the printed edition is public domain as above. The text layer is machine OCR (tesseract, Sanskrit) and is not proofread. The same scan as archive.org `prasnamarga035823mbp`, whose text layer was OCRed as Telugu and is unreadable (fetched first, 5,075,284 bytes, then discarded).
sources.use: Reference only: OCR read in the lab, cited by chapter and verse number. Nothing of the text is exported.

sources.work: The Brihat Jataka of Varaha Mihira, translated into English by N. Chidambaram Iyer
sources.author: N. Chidambaram Iyer (translator; death year not recorded)
sources.workStatus: Public domain, United States: verified (published 1885). India: inferred, not verified; accepted by the owner on 2026-09-30 on the same footing as Benham. India's term is life + 60 years, so the translation would still be protected there only if its translator died in 1966 or later. His death year is not recorded; surviving to 1966 would mean living 81 years after publishing it. The lab applies the test it applied to Benham and Dale and treats the book as public domain. The Wellcome Library copy is released under the Public Domain Mark.
sources.edition: Madras: Foster Press, 1885 (Wellcome Library copy, 236 pages)
sources.licence: Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0 (archive.org item metadata, Wellcome Library copy).
sources.use: English reading aid for the Bṛhajjātaka; quotable (public domain). Rules cite the Sanskrit verse number.

sources.work: The Practice of Palmistry for Professional Purposes, vol. 2
sources.author: Comte C. de Saint-Germain (pseudonym of Edgar de Valcourt-Vermont, born 1846)
sources.date: Chicago: The French-American Publishing Company, 1897 (copyright 1897, The National School of Palmistry)
sources.workStatus: Public domain, United States: verified (US publication, 1897). India: established by the author's birth year - the Library of Congress authority is 'Valcourt-Vermont, E. de (Edgar), 1846-', with no death year; life + 60 would still run only if he had died in 1966 or later, at the age of 119 or more. The task's 'd. 1921' could not be confirmed in any authority record and is not relied on.
sources.edition: Chicago: The French-American Publishing Company, 1897, volume 2, printed pp. 194-413 (Google scan of the Harvard College Library copy, 245 images)
sources.licence: possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT (archive.org item metadata; Google scan).
sources.use: Palmistry source for the life-question rules; quotable (public domain).

consideredNotUsed.what: The only digital copies found: uploads of P. S. Sastri's 20th-century English and Hindi translations
consideredNotUsed.why: No transcription of the Sanskrit was found on GRETIL, sanskritdocuments.org, sa.wikisource or github.com/sanskrit/raw_etexts. The translations are modern and not public domain (one upload asserts a Public Domain Mark without basis). Not fetched; NO rules were extracted from this text. House and planet significations, its usual use, are cited from BPHS and the Phaladīpikā instead.
